title: Find the leaking core of an armoured cable: crank the insulation tester with one hand, probe each core with the other
instruction: One core of this armoured cable leaks to the armour. The tester's earth lead is already on the earth stud, which is bonded to the armour. Keep the tester's crank turning at least 0.8 turns a second with one hand, and with the other hold the red prod on each core's stud in turn until the needle settles: test all three cores before touching any flag. Then tip back the flag in front of the core whose needle stayed away from infinity, put the prod back in its slotted rest and let go of everything.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00) insulation-test cables before switching them on and when tracing a fault: each core against earth at 500 V DC, where BS 7671 asks for at least 1 megohm. On a hand-crank tester (a megger) the test voltage exists only while the generator handle turns, so one hand keeps cranking while the other holds the line prod on each core in turn, and the needle is read before moving on. In an armoured cable the steel wire armour is the earth: it is bonded at the gland to the earth stud that carries the tester's earth lead, so a core whose insulation leaks to the armour pulls the needle off infinity. The robot must keep a steady crank going with one arm while placing a prod tip on 6 mm studs with the other, read a dial, and mark only the core that failed; guessing scores nothing because the leaking core changes from trial to trial.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the bench (x forward, y left); heights above the bench. Insulation tester: ZC25-3 hand-crank megohmmeter (500 V DC, 0-500 megohm; maker's size 205 x 120 x 145 mm, about 2 kg, crank rated 120 r/min), grey steel case standing fixed with its long side toward the robot, centred x 30.0, y -8.75. Its crank is on the right end face (y -19.0): a horizontal shaft 8.5 high, a 6.0 cm black steel arm and a black free-turning plastic handle 1.4 cm across and 5.5 cm long, starting toward the robot (handle centre x 24.0, y -23.2, 8.5 high). Its dial is on top: a white scale 9.0 x 7.2 cm with a black needle 4.5 cm long pivoting at x 27.0, y -9.75 (infinity at the needle's left end, zero at its right; marks at both ends and mid-scale). Terminals on top at its left end: LINE (red cap, x 26.5), EARTH (black, x 33.5), GUARD between (not used). Cable: 3-core 1.5 mm2 XLPE/SWA/PVC to BS 5467 (black sheath 12.6 mm across; brown, black and grey cores; galvanised steel wire armour), laid along x at y 12.5, 3.5 high, from a closed grey steel box (10 x 10 x 6 cm, x 58-68) to a brass CW20S gland in a 3 mm steel gland plate at x 34.2. The gland's brass earth tag bonds the armour, by a green/yellow lead, to the earth stud; the tester's EARTH lead (black) runs from its EARTH terminal to the same stud. Terminal block: brown phenolic, 4 x 14 x 1.5 cm, at x 28-32, y 3.75-17.75, with four brass M6 studs at x 30 (nut 1.1 cm across, stud end 0.6 cm across, top 2.6 high): y 5.5 earth (green/yellow mark), 9.0 brown core, 12.5 black, 16.0 grey; each core's crimped ring lug is under its nut. Phenolic barriers 1.2 high between studs. The leak: inside the far box the cores are cut back and kept apart; a 0.5 megohm 1 W resistor joins one core to the armour. Which core is set by the trial seed (seed mod 3: 0 brown, 1 black, 2 grey) and nothing outside the box shows it; the other two cores read infinity (over 500 megohm). Flags: three red aluminium flags 2.0 x 4.2 cm, 3 mm thick, upright on pins 1.8 high at x 26.2 in front of the core studs; each tips back (away from the robot) to a 50 degree stop and stays where left (0.02 N m pin friction). Prod: red test prod 14 cm long (body 1.1 cm across, finger guard 1.8 cm across 1.6 cm above its 2 mm steel tip), 35 g; its lead to the LINE terminal is not simulated. It stands in its rest, a dark grey plastic cup at x 24.0, y 24.5 with a 2.6 cm square bore 4 cm deep above its floor, the floor 3.0 high with a 1 cm slot the tip goes through; the finger guard sits on the floor. Safe isolation: the cable is connected to no supply at either end; the only source is the tester itself.
scoring: Measured with a ruler, a protractor and a stopwatch (in simulation from the poses). A core counts as tested once the prod's tip has rested on its stud's brass (within 6 mm of the stud's axis, no more than 2.5 mm above the stud's top and not below the nut's top, prod within 30 degrees of vertical) for 1 s in a row while the crank turned at 0.8 rev/s or more (averaged over the last 0.5 s). A flag counts as tipped at 25 degrees or more. Score 0 if any flag is tipped before all three cores have been tested (this stays 0 for the trial), if a healthy core's flag is tipped, or if no core was tested. Otherwise 0.25 for one or two cores tested; 0.5 for all three tested but the leaking core's flag not tipped; 0.75 for all three tested and only the leaking core's flag tipped, but the prod not back in its rest (tip within the floor's slot, finger guard within 4 mm of the floor, leaning 20 degrees or less: the cup holds it within about 16), a gripper within 5 cm of the prod's grip, the crank handle or any flag's top, or something still moving (prod over 1 cm/s, crank over 0.5 rad/s, a flag over 0.1 rad/s); 1.0 when all of that holds for 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the prod in its rest, turn the crank handle back toward the robot and set every flag upright. Out of the robot's sight, open the far box, move the 0.5 megohm resistor to the core the next trial's seed picks (seed mod 3) and close the lid; check by hand that this core reads about 0.5 megohm and the others infinity. After each trial touch each core's stud to the earth stud to discharge the cable.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; crank, handle and flags are friction hinges. No current flows: the needle and 'tested' are computed from the crank's speed and where the prod tip rests, against the trial's leak. The needle answers only at 0.8 rev/s or more (maker's rated speed 120 r/min, beyond this arm). Needle drawn 5 mm wide to show at 320 px. Prod lead not simulated; tester fixed (2 kg). Estimates: crank radius, shaft height, handle, crank drag 0.09 N m at 1 rev/s, scale mid 5 megohm, block, flags, rest, prod.
